career_spells.employer: Australian Parliament — employing department to confirm
career_spells.evidence_note: Rebello's member biography and first speech describe work as a parliamentary attendant sorting mail and supporting the House chamber. In a 2026 interview he said he was about 19, and a later post described the work as roughly ten years before 2025. Exact dates, hours, employment basis and leave are unpublished. Revisited member biography and speech confirm attendant/mail work but do not name employing department. Earlier record assigned Department of Parliamentary Services without an explicit supporting passage; retain that as a verification lead, not established employer identity.
career_spells.counting_note: Public employment is supported, but no countable full-time interval is established.

career_spells.employer: Office of the Minister for Foreign Affairs, the Hon. Julie Bishop MP
career_spells.evidence_note: Public professional-profile evidence explicitly dates Julie Bishop office July2017–September2018. Earlier sources confirm the role. A 2025 legal-industry interview says Rebello deferred his KWM graduate program temporarily for this office, supporting the sequence but not a full-time status, exact day boundary, title or leave allocation.
career_spells.counting_note: Political staff employment is excluded irrespective of public funding.

career_spells.role: Solicitor, foreign investment law; member of Solicitors Assisting team for2020Bushfires Royal Commission
career_spells.evidence_note: The official biography says only 'Solicitor'. Rebello and party profiles identify King & Wood Mallesons and foreign-investment specialization; a March 2025 Lawyers Weekly profile says he had worked there for the past six years and remained a solicitor while campaigning. A user-supplied screenshot of his public professional profile displays Solicitor, October2019–June2025, after the separately recorded graduate program. Public first-person post confirms admission in ACT Supreme Court, but only relative publication age is accessible. Hours, leave, secondments, exact day boundaries and the May–June2025 overlap with elected office remain unresolved. April2025 interview describes practising law retrospectively and full-time candidacy since April2024, so KWM profile-title tenure cannot establish continuous active work through June2025. His first-person account of Bushfires Royal Commission work is now corroborated by its28October2020Appendix2, printed p45, which lists him specifically under Solicitors Assisting. KWM primary practice history confirms the firm supplied solicitors assisting; attribution to his established KWM employment is supported by these combined sources. This is a nested2020legal assignment, not an additional duration or proof of government payroll/secondment. Personal assignment start/end, hours and leave remain unknown; Commission-wide dates are not substituted for his boundaries.
career_spells.counting_note: Substantive private legal work and month boundaries are supported, but unknown hours, leave and overlap with elected office prevent treating the whole interval as countable full-time work.
